vocab.gloss: to feel relieved; to feel reassured; to be at ease

example.pinyin: nǐ fàngxīn, wǒ yídìng zhǔnshí dào.
example.gloss: Don't worry, I'll definitely be there on time.

example.pinyin: cǎodì shàng yǒu hěn duō rén zài wán.
example.gloss: There are a lot of people playing on the grass.

example.pinyin: zhè bēi chá tài tián le.
example.gloss: This cup of tea is too sweet.

example.pinyin: wǒ hái méi zuò wán zuòyè.
example.gloss: I haven't finished my homework yet.

vocab.gloss: thin; to lose weight; (of clothing) tight

example.pinyin: tā zuìjìn shòu le hěn duō.
example.gloss: He has lost a lot of weight recently.

vocab.gloss: green; (slang) (derived from 绿帽子) to cheat on (one's spouse or boyfriend or girlfriend)

example.hanzi: 我買了一雙綠色的鞋子。
example.pinyin: wǒ mǎi le yì shuāng lǜsè de xiézi.
example.gloss: I bought a pair of green shoes.

grammar.title: 讓 + 某人 + 放心 (to put someone at ease)
grammar.pattern: A + 讓 + B + (很/不太) + 放心
grammar.explanation: 用「讓」說明某件事或某個人使別人的心情變得安心。動詞「放心」前面可以加「很」或「不太」。這是台灣日常生活中很常用的說法。

examples.hanzi: 他做事很認真，讓老闆很放心。
examples.pinyin: tā zuò shì hěn rènzhēn, ràng lǎobǎn hěn fàngxīn.
examples.gloss: He works conscientiously, which puts the boss at ease.

examples.hanzi: 弟弟的成績讓爸爸很放心。
examples.pinyin: dìdi de chéngjī ràng bàba hěn fàngxīn.
examples.gloss: My little brother's grades put Dad at ease.

examples.hanzi: 你自己騎腳踏車去，媽媽不太放心。
examples.pinyin: nǐ zìjǐ qí jiǎotàchē qù, māma bú tài fàngxīn.
examples.gloss: Mom isn't quite at ease with you riding a bike there by yourself.

dialogue.speaker: 媽媽
dialogue.pinyin: nǐ de zuòyè zuò wán le ma?

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.pinyin: zuò wán le, nǐ fàngxīn la!

dialogue.speaker: 媽媽
dialogue.hanzi: 那我們去公園走走，那邊的草很綠喔。
dialogue.pinyin: nà wǒmen qù gōngyuán zǒu zǒu, nà biān de cǎo hěn lǜ ō.
dialogue.gloss: Then let's go for a walk in the park; the grass over there is really green.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 好啊！我想吃甜的，可以買西瓜嗎？
dialogue.pinyin: hǎo a! wǒ xiǎng chī tián de, kěyǐ mǎi xīguā ma?
dialogue.gloss: Sure! I want something sweet — can we buy a watermelon?

dialogue.speaker: 媽媽
dialogue.hanzi: 可以，你最近瘦了，多吃一點。
dialogue.pinyin: kěyǐ, nǐ zuìjìn shòu le, duō chī yìdiǎn.
dialogue.gloss: Sure. You've gotten thinner lately, so eat a bit more.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 謝謝媽媽，我們騎腳踏車去吧！
dialogue.pinyin: xièxie māma, wǒmen qí jiǎotàchē qù ba!
dialogue.gloss: Thanks, Mom. Let's ride our bikes there!

sentences.gloss: The grass in the park is very green.

sentences.pinyin: wǒ zuò wán zuòyè jiù qù wán.
sentences.gloss: I'll go play as soon as I finish my homework.

sentences.pinyin: mèimei zuìjìn shòu le hěn duō.
sentences.gloss: My little sister has gotten a lot thinner lately.
This way Mom can feel at ease.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bàba zuì ài hē bīng píjiǔ.
example.gloss: My dad loves drinking cold beer the most.
This piece of cake is really delicious!

vocab.gloss: to feel sad; to feel unwell; (of life) to be difficult

example.hanzi: 他考得不好,心裡很難過。
example.pinyin: Tā kǎo de bù hǎo, xīnlǐ hěn nánguò.
example.gloss: He didn't do well on the test and feels really sad.

example.pinyin: Wǎnshàng diàn lǐ de kèrén hěn duō.
example.gloss: There are a lot of customers in the shop in the evening.

vocab.gloss: (informal) grandma (paternal grandmother); (respectful) mistress of the house; (coll.) boobies

example.pinyin: Wǒ nǎinai zuò de miàn zuì hǎochī.
example.gloss: The noodles my grandma makes are the best.

grammar.title: 用「讓」表示某事使人有某種感覺
grammar.pattern: A + 讓 + B + 感覺/狀態
grammar.explanation: 「讓」here means "to make (someone feel a certain way)". A is the thing or person that causes the feeling, B is the one who feels it, and after B comes an adjective or a verb phrase like 很難過、很開心、很想哭. This is very common in everyday Taiwan Mandarin.

examples.pinyin: Zuótiān de shì ràng wǒ hěn nánguò.
examples.gloss: What happened yesterday made me really sad.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶做的蛋糕讓客人都很開心。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zuò de dàngāo ràng kèrén dōu hěn kāixīn.
examples.gloss: The cake grandma made made all the guests happy.

examples.hanzi: 這杯冰啤酒讓我覺得很舒服。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi bīng píjiǔ ràng wǒ juéde hěn shūfú.
examples.gloss: This cold beer makes me feel great.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 奶奶,晚上有客人要來嗎?
dialogue.pinyin: Nǎinai, wǎnshàng yǒu kèrén yào lái ma?

dialogue.speaker: 奶奶
dialogue.pinyin: Duì a, nǐ gēge yào lái chīfàn.
dialogue.gloss: Yes, your older brother is coming for dinner.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 那我去買一個蛋糕,再買兩瓶啤酒。
dialogue.pinyin: Nà wǒ qù mǎi yí ge dàngāo, zài mǎi liǎng píng píjiǔ.
dialogue.gloss: Then I'll go buy a cake and two bottles of beer.

dialogue.speaker: 奶奶
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo, yú yě yào mǎi xīnxiān de o.
dialogue.gloss: OK, and buy fresh fish too.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 沒問題!上次哥哥沒來,你很難過。
dialogue.pinyin: Méi wèntí! Shàng cì gēge méi lái, nǐ hěn nánguò.
dialogue.gloss: No problem! Last time my brother didn't come, you were really sad.

dialogue.speaker: 奶奶
dialogue.hanzi: 是啊,這次他來,我最開心了。
dialogue.pinyin: Shì a, zhè cì tā lái, wǒ zuì kāixīn le.
dialogue.gloss: Yes, this time he's coming, so I'm the happiest.

sentences.pinyin: Nǎinai zuò de dàngāo zuì hǎochī.
sentences.gloss: The cake grandma makes is the tastiest.
Dad likes to drink beer in the evening.

sentences.pinyin: Jiā lǐ lái le sān ge kèrén.

sentences.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì ràng wǒ hěn nánguò.

grammar.title: Saying where an action happens: 在 + place + verb
grammar.explanation: In Chinese, the place where an action happens comes BEFORE the verb, not after it. Use 在 + place, then the verb phrase. So 'I wash bowls in the kitchen' becomes 我在廚房刷碗 (I + at kitchen + wash bowls). Putting the place after the verb sounds wrong.

examples.pinyin: wǒ zài chú fáng shuā wǎn.
examples.gloss: I wash the bowls in the kitchen.

examples.hanzi: 爺爺在房間裡練習寫字。
examples.pinyin: yé ye zài fáng jiān lǐ liàn xí xiě zì.
examples.gloss: Grandpa practices writing characters in his room.

examples.pinyin: tā měi tiān zài jiā liàn xí shù xué.
examples.gloss: She practices math at home every day.

dialogue.hanzi: 小明，你可以幫我刷碗嗎？
dialogue.pinyin: xiǎo míng, nǐ kě yǐ bāng wǒ shuā wǎn ma?
dialogue.gloss: Xiaoming, can you help me wash the bowls?

dialogue.gloss: Sure, I'll go to the kitchen right now.

dialogue.pinyin: xiè xie. shuā wán wǎn zài qù liàn xí shù xué o.

dialogue.gloss: Then I'll wash the bowls first, and go for a walk with Grandpa later.
